newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks cautiously higher after no rate action.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks cautiously higher after no rate action.

text.p: U.S. blue chip shares rebounded after the Federal Reserve left short-term interest rates unchanged.

U.S. economists had been split over whether the Fed would ratchet up a key overnight bank lending rate, the federal funds rate, or leave rates unchanged at a meeting in Washington today of the Federal Open Market Committee.
The Dow Jones industrial average erased a loss of 20 points and quickly moved to a gain of 30 points before settling back slightly. The average was up 10 points to 7239 at 1447 EDT/1847 GMT.
The Standard & Poor's 500 Index was barely positive, up 0.11 to 833.4. The Nasdaq composite, firm for much of the day, was up nearly 10 to 1351.

On the New York Stock Exchange, breadth was almost evenly split with a slight edge going to losing stocks. Declines led advances 12 to 11. Volume was about 333.9 million shares in late afternoon trading.
